capabilities: Scan and classify vault notes into project, decision, research, review, and chat-export types
Extract facts, decisions, actions, risks, assumptions, questions, and insights from notes
Write Markdown and JSON context-pack artifacts with coverage, provenance, and confidence stats
Diff consecutive compiles via a manifest to surface added, changed, stale, and resolved context
Expose compilation as CLI commands and MCP tools for AI clients
disambiguation: Despite the name, it is not a life-management OS or AI assistant; it makes no LLM calls and only compiles vault notes into context-pack artifacts.
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The Obsidian adapter is desktop-only; the same compiler is also available as @gotsaeng/cli and @gotsaeng/mcp on npm. The README includes an explicit 'What GotSaeng OS Does Not Do' section and a security/privacy statement (local-only, no telemetry).
motivation: The author built it because LLMs are useful but long-running work still loses context, and scattered notes, chat exports, and decisions are often forgotten; a local-first compiler turns that scattered Markdown into a portable handoff pack.
problem: Long-running work loses context because notes, chat exports, decisions, and execution logs live in separate places, and Obsidian has no way to compile them into a portable handoff pack.

requires.name: MCP client such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor

summary: Vault compiler that scans Markdown notes, extracts facts, decisions, and actions, and writes auditable Markdown/JSON context packs for humans and AI tools.
